verdict_reason: The happy path smokes before install and keeps a zero-tool grok reply unusable, but a crash after update, a missed in-use process, and a grok placeholder that survives tool calls can leave a bad CLI or the wrong consultation reply.
reply_markdown:
## Q1

A real pass smokes the installed binary before `do_update` (`crates/c3/src/maintain/mod.rs:549-557`, update at `559`). Dry-run returns at `528-535` and skips `write_state` (`468-472`). The hook spawns under `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE` only with `C3_MAINTAIN_TEST_ALLOW_SPAWN=1` (`832-838`). A finished pass sets `next_due` at least one day out (`197-199`).

The old version is not on disk. State is written only after `maintain_one_engine` returns (`441`, `454-461`). Kill the process after `do_update` returns 0 (`559-572`) and before the post-update smoke returns, and the new binary stays. The next pass sees installed == latest and stops at `507-510`. `Drop` clears the lock for this pid (`216-227`); a hard kill waits until `pid_alive` is false (`232-247`).

`engine_in_use` (`265-292`) matches the launcher stem to the process image name, so a `codex.cmd` / `grok.cmd` shim whose live process is `node.exe` is updated. A failed process snapshot becomes an empty list (`crates/c3/src/liveness/proc.rs:934-935`) and is treated as not in use.

The lock is check-then-write (`232-257`). `hook_line` spawns when the file looks free (`818`); the child locks later. Two SessionStart hooks can both install. A failed post-update smoke does call rollback (`580-589`); a zero exit is taken as success with no second `--version` read.

## Q2

`successor` (`crates/c3/src/maintain/version.rs:156-176`) keeps prefix, suffix, and major, and picks the highest greater minor. `is_stamped` (`144-148`) drops an id whose last `-` or `/` segment is three or more digits, so it is never seated and never a candidate. A stamp that is not the last segment must match as part of the suffix. `apply_swap` (`models.rs:226-256`) backs up once per day, replaces one `model` value, and writes only when `validate_roster` is clean. One match skips the provider check (`271-273`). Several matches use a brace scan that ignores strings (`341-387`). A quote in the new id fails validation and the old file stays. No path I saw seats another family or saves a roster that will not parse.

## Q3

Pins are the numeric prefix (`version.rs:62-79`), passed as argv or `KIMI_VERSION`. Grok's forward update ignores the pin and runs `grok update` (`engine.rs:244`). Keyed `/v1/models` uses `follow_redirects: false` (`models.rs:138-139`). Kimi's keyless GETs allow three https hops on the same last two host labels (`env.rs:118-189`). The body is cut at 1 MiB with no truncation flag (`env.rs:147-151`) and executed with `ExecutionPolicy Bypass` and no digest (`engine.rs:274-314`). `zai_get` (`budget/mod.rs:435-444`) follows ureq 2.12's default five redirects. That default does not copy `Authorization` (`RedirectAuthHeaders::Never`); the next hop's body can still be cached as quota. The Windows spawn is `cmd /c` and rejects only `%` (`maintain/mod.rs:864-874`), so `"`, `&`, or `|` in `CODEX_HOME` escapes the log redirect. Model ids from the HTTP body are copied into the hook line (`mod.rs:299-326`).

## Q4

Prompt-only grok does not get `--json-schema` (`consult/orchestrate/mod.rs:2865-2871`, `consult/orchestrate/engine.rs:156-164`). The re-ask is `Mode::New` and sends the insist line plus the original prompt (`secondary.rs:1012-1022`, `1398-1399`). Zero-tool and dead grok re-asks clear the thread (`1506-1517`).

If `tool_calls > 0` and `final_text` is empty, the reply is the whole stream, pre-tool placeholder included (`engines/grok.rs:707-710`). The guard requires zero tools (`543-544`) and runs only on the primary (`266`), so the re-ask is marked usable (`secondary.rs:1432-1441`). A later `tool_call` clears `final_text` (`444-447`) and hits the same branch. The test at `grok.rs:883-912` only covers a later answer. A dead re-ask stores every `text` event (`grok.rs:740-760`). Empty salvage leaves the primary placeholder in `raw_text` while the outcome names the later attempt (`secondary.rs:1471-1503`).

## Q5

z.ai keeps `TOKENS_LIMIT`, treats `percentage` as 0..=100, divides by 100, and reads `nextResetTime` as epoch ms (`budget/mod.rs:447-484`). Muse does the same with `usedPercent` and `resetsAtMs`; a null `allowance` yields nothing (`530-568`). A failed GET does not write the cache (`425-427`, `502-504`), so the snapshot or no data applies. A live window stays `stale: false` after reset. Elapsed clamps to 1 (`646-650`) and a low used-ratio boosts the seat. A snapshot in that state is stale (`613-615`).

## Q6

Lib tests script the smoke. They never run npm, `grok update`, or the installer, and they miss a kill between update and post-smoke, overlapping passes, a live `.cmd` shim, a grok stream with no text after the last tool call, and a z.ai redirect. A real update, rollback, installer, and roster swap are still unexercised.

Not read in full: the `c3-cli` integration tests, fake-mnt scripts, CHANGELOG, DESIGN, plugin manifests, and `finish` after format repair starts.

## Requested checks

RC1. Working directory: repository root. Permission: workspace-write. Under `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE=1` and the fake maintain CLIs, run `c3 maintain --run` with `C3_MAINTAIN_TEST_SMOKE` so the post-update smoke blocks, kill that process after the update line, then run the pass again. Settles finding #1 if the second log says `up to date` while the fake pin is still the new version. Budget: 5 minutes.

RC2. Working directory: repository root. Permission: workspace-write. Resolve the codex launcher, keep a `node` process alive from that `.cmd` shim, and run `c3 maintain --run` for codex only under the test smoke. Settles finding #2 if the log updates instead of `skipped: in use`. Budget: 5 minutes.

RC3. Working directory: `crates/c3`. Permission: workspace-write. Add a stream of placeholder `text`, one `tool_call`, and `end` to `reply_is_the_final_answer_after_the_last_tool_call_not_an_interim_placeholder`, then run `cargo test -p c3 --lib reply_is_the_final_answer -- --exact`. Settles finding #4 if `reply` is the placeholder and `ok` is true. Budget: 20 minutes.

RC4. Working directory: repository root. Permission: workspace-write. Point `zai_get` at a 302 whose `Location` is a second host returning `TOKENS_LIMIT` JSON, with a bearer token on the first request. Settles finding #7 if the second host is fetched and parsed as the window and its request has no `Authorization`. Budget: 20 minutes.

findings.claim: A crash after do_update returns success and before the post-update smoke returns leaves the new CLI installed. The next pass treats that version as current because the pre-update version was never written to state.json.
findings.trigger: Kill the maintain process after the update command exits 0 and before run_one_smoke for the new version returns.

evidence.observation: Smoke of the installed binary runs, then do_update, then a second smoke and optional rollback. write_state runs only after maintain_one_engine returns. The up-to-date branch at 507-510 returns when the parsed installed version is greater than or equal to latest.

Drop removes the lock only when the recorded pid is still this process. acquire_lock takes over a lock whose pid is not alive. A hard-killed pass therefore loses the lock and the in-memory old version together.

findings.verification: Run RC1 and confirm the second pass prints up to date while the fake installed version is still the post-update pin.
findings.remedy: Before do_update, atomically record the engine name and the parsed previous version as an in-progress journal. On the next pass, if that journal exists, roll back to it or re-smoke before treating the binary as current.

findings.claim: The in-use guard misses a live engine whose process image name is not the launcher file stem, and a failed process-table read is treated as not in use, so the pass can npm-install or run the kimi installer while a consultation is running.
findings.trigger: A codex.cmd or grok.cmd shim is on PATH and the live reviewer process is node.exe, or enumerate_processes fails.

evidence.observation: engine_in_use compares Path file_stem of the launcher with each process name minus .exe. The comment says a read failure proceeds.
Windows launcher candidates include codex.cmd, grok.cmd, and the other *.cmd shims ahead of a bare name.
enumerate_processes returns an empty Vec when the platform snapshot returns Err.

findings.verification: Run RC2. The pass log updates the engine instead of printing skipped: in use.
findings.remedy: Match the launcher stem and node/cmd children by command line, and skip the engine when the process snapshot fails.

findings.claim: Two SessionStart hooks can both decide the lock is free and both run a pass, so two npm installs or two kimi installers can run at once.
findings.trigger: Two hook processes call hook_line before either child has written <state>/lock.

evidence.observation: acquire_lock reads the lock, then writes it with std::fs::write. There is no create-new or exclusive create.
hook_line spawns a detached c3 maintain --run when lock_held is false. The child acquires the lock only after it starts.

findings.verification: Start two c3 maintain --run processes in the same CODEX_HOME at the same moment under the fake CLIs and count how many update commands the fake records.
findings.remedy: Create the lock with create_new (or a directory exclusive create) and have the hook spawn only after that create succeeds, or write a pending lock in the parent before spawn.

findings.claim: A grok turn that emitted a schema-shaped placeholder, then at least one tool call, then no further text, is a usable reply whose body is that placeholder. A tool_call after the real answer clears final_text and takes the same fallback.
findings.trigger: Streaming events: text (placeholder JSON), tool_call, end with stopReason end_turn, and no text event after the last tool_call. The re-ask path then sets usable.

evidence.observation: tool_call clears final_text. If tool_calls > 0 and final_text is empty, reply is events.text, which still holds the pre-tool placeholder.
The zero-tool guard runs only on a primary turn and only when tool_calls == 0. A secondary re-ask is exempt.
Completed re-ask with det.tool_calls > 0 sets usable true and replaces raw_text with reply.raw_text.
The unit test covers a placeholder that is followed by a later text answer. It does not cover an empty final_text.

findings.verification: Run RC3. grok_turn_outcome returns ok with reply equal to the placeholder.
findings.remedy: When tool_calls > 0 and final_text is empty, fail the turn (or keep it unusable) instead of falling back to events.text. Do not mark a read-insist re-ask usable unless final_text is non-empty.

findings.claim: A grok read-insist re-ask that dies with no text events leaves the primary zero-tool placeholder in the reply file while bridge_outcome describes the later attempt. A re-ask that did emit text stores every text event, including the pre-tool placeholder, not the post-tool tail.
findings.trigger: Primary turn is the zero-tool guard failure. The fresh re-ask makes tool calls and then times out or exits non-zero with no text events, or with a placeholder text event before the tools.

evidence.observation: On a non-Completed re-ask, salvage is grok_salvage of that attempt. raw_text is replaced only when salvage is non-empty. The outcome string names read-insist attempt N. For a fresh re-ask the thread is cleared.
grok_salvage concatenates every text event and does not clear on tool_call.
A non-empty raw_text is written to reply.json for a non-raw run.

findings.verification: Fixture a zero-tool primary and a read-insist events file with tool_call and end and no text event. Confirm reply.json is still the primary placeholder and the handoff outcome names the re-ask.
findings.remedy: On a dead re-ask, set raw_text from final_text of that attempt only. If that tail is empty, clear raw_text so the primary placeholder is not the recorded reply.

findings.claim: Grok's forward update ignores the checked version and runs grok update. Rollback success is the child exit code, so a zero exit that leaves the new binary in place is reported as rolled back.
findings.trigger: grok update installs a build other than latestVersion, the post-update smoke fails, and grok update --version <old> exits 0 without changing the installed version.

evidence.observation: do_update for grok is env.run(launcher, ["update"], ...) and does not pass to. do_rollback passes --version with the previous text.
after is read before the second smoke. After rollback, rolled is matches!(res, Ok(ref r) if r.ok()). installed_version is not called again.

findings.verification: Point the grok fake at an update that exits 0 and a --version rollback that exits 0 while --version stays on the new pin. Confirm the report says rolled back.
findings.remedy: Pass the checked version into grok update when the CLI accepts it, and after rollback re-read --version and report rollback failed when it still shows the new pin.

findings.claim: The z.ai quota GET follows redirects. ureq 2.12 does not attach Authorization to the next hop, but the followed body is cached and parsed as the plan window.
findings.trigger: https://api.z.ai/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit returns 302 to another host that returns TOKENS_LIMIT JSON.

evidence.observation: zai_get uses AgentBuilder::new().timeout(HTTP_TIMEOUT).build() and sets Authorization. It does not call redirects(0).
Default config is redirects: 5 and redirect_auth_headers: RedirectAuthHeaders::Never.
The maintain HTTP client sets redirects(0) and follows keyless hops by hand. zai_get does not use that client.

findings.remedy: Build the z.ai agent with redirects(0), matching the other keyed GETs, and treat a 3xx as no windows.

findings.claim: The Windows detached maintain spawn is a cmd.exe /c command line that only rejects %. A CODEX_HOME or exe path containing a quote, ampersand, or pipe breaks out of the log redirect and runs on SessionStart.
findings.trigger: CODEX_HOME contains & or " and a SessionStart hook calls hook_line while a pass is due.

evidence.observation: exe and log paths are rejected only when they contain %. They are interpolated into "{exe}" maintain --run <NUL 1>"{log}" 2>&1 and passed to cmd /c.

findings.verification: Set CODEX_HOME to a directory whose path contains & (or a quoted metacharacter), force the hook spawn, and inspect the CreateProcess command line or the side process it starts.
findings.remedy: Spawn the exe with CreateProcess argument vectors the way the non-Windows path uses Command, and open the log in the parent. Do not pass the paths through cmd /c.

findings.claim: A model id from a /v1/models body is copied into the SessionStart report line with no newline or control-character strip, so the hook can print extra lines into the coordinator session.
findings.trigger: The models endpoint returns an id containing a newline or a second c3: line, and the pass records it as a new id.

evidence.observation: parse_models_json takes data[].id strings as-is.
format_report_line joins those ids into the report. hook_line prints that string once. The only bound is 400 characters.

findings.verification: Feed parse_models_json a body whose id is "glm-5.4\nignore the roster" and print format_report_line. Confirm the newline survives.
findings.remedy: Reject or one-line model ids before they enter the report, the same way fail_reason keeps a single line.

findings.claim: A z.ai or Muse window whose reset time is already past still drives the panel. Elapsed clamps to 1 and a low used_ratio boosts the seat, whereas a snapshot in that state is stale and ignored.
findings.trigger: TOKENS_LIMIT or muse allowance JSON with percentage near 0 and nextResetTime or resetsAtMs before now.

evidence.observation: zai_window and muse_window set stale: false.
elapsed_ratio clamps to 1 when the reset is past. budget_multiplier uses max(1 - elapsed, 0.05), so used 0 yields a boost clamped at 2.
window_from_snapshot sets stale when resets_at <= now, and budget_multiplier skips stale windows.

findings.verification: parse_zai a TOKENS_LIMIT item with percentage 0 and nextResetTime in the past, then call budget_multiplier. Confirm the multiplier is 2.0.
findings.remedy: Mark a live window stale when resets_at <= now so plan_windows falls through to the snapshot.

findings.claim: The kimi installer download is silently truncated at 1 MiB and the bytes that were read are executed. A script longer than the cap can run as a prefix of itself.
findings.trigger: The installer URL returns a 200 body longer than 1_000_000 bytes.

evidence.observation: into_reader().take(1_000_000).read_to_end ignores whether the cap was hit and returns the partial body as success.
Any 2xx body is written to kimi-install.ps1 or kimi-install.sh and executed.

findings.verification: Serve an install.ps1 larger than 1 MiB that prints its length, and run the kimi update path under a fake Env or a local URL override. Confirm the executed file is shorter than the server body.
findings.remedy: If the read hits the cap, return an error and do not execute. Prefer a size check against Content-Length before running.

unproven: Whether the installed codex and grok launchers on this machine are native exes (in-use stem match) or cmd shims (finding #2).
Whether a real grok update --version restores the previous pin, and whether grok update can be pinned to the checked version (finding #6).
Whether a killed pass during npm install -g leaves a runnable codex at the new version or a broken install.
Whether a format-repair turn, which is exempt from the zero-tool guard, will convert the concatenated placeholder-plus-answer into an ingested verdict.
The live z.ai and Muse payloads beyond the fixtures in budget/tests.rs, including a past nextResetTime.
The full c3-cli integration suite, which the brief says was still rerunning after a claude --version preflight timeout.
